title: Multisensory hypersensitivity – a chronic pain marker
summary:
The study aims to investigate two chronically painful conditions, namely the so-called Fibromyalgia Syndrome and somatoform pain disorders, which have been insufficiently understood in their development.

Using modern imaging techniques (Magnetic Resonance Imaging, MRI), brain structures and activities will be examined to differentiate between individuals with chronic pain and healthy subjects. In this context, we are drawing upon the phenomenon known as multisensory hypersensitivity, which occurs in various chronic pain syndromes. This phenomenon, where individuals perceive not only painful stimuli but also, for example, smells, sounds, and visual impressions more intensely, could be an indication that there is a particular characteristic in the brain responsible for certain chronic pain disorders.
conditions: The study examines patients with various chronic pain conditions. The first group of patients consists of individuals diagnosed with Fibromyalgia Syndrome (ICD-10: M79.70). The patients in the second group have both a diagnosis of Fibromyalgia Syndrome and Small Fiber Neuropathy (ICD-10: G62.88). The third group of patients exclusively has Small Fiber Neuropathy, and the fourth group of patients has a somatoform pain disorder (ICD-10: F45.-).

interventions.name:
Patients with a diagnosed fibromyalgia syndrome (FMS)

Twenty patients diagnosed with fibromyalgia syndrome between the ages of 18 and 60 will be included. The patients will be recruited in collaboration with the Department of Nephrology and Hypertension, Rheumatological and Immunological Diseases

Patients with a diagnosed fibromyalgia syndrome and additionally a small-fiber-neuropathy

Twenty patients between the ages of 18 and 60 will also be included in this group. We will recruit this group of patients in collaboration with the Department of Neurology at the University Hospital Aachen.

Patients diagnosed with a small-fiber-neuropathy.

In this group, 20 patients between the ages of 18 and 60 will also be included, and the patient registry of the Department of Neurology will also be involved in the recruitment.

For Arm 3, the same examinations as in Arm 1 will be conducted.

Patients with a somatoform pain disorder

Twenty patients between the ages of 18 and 60 will also be included in this group. The patients will be recruited from the Department of Psychiatry, Psychotherapy, and Psychosomatics at the University Hospital Aachen

Healthy Controls

20 healthy control subjects between the ages of 18 and 60 will also be included in this group. 

For Arm 5, the same examinations as in Arm 1 will be conducted.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1) Ability to provide written informed consent after being informed.
2) Willingness to complete all study procedures.
3) Fulfillment of specific diagnostic criteria (depending on the patient group).
Exclusion criteria:
1) Metals or metal-containing devices that are in constant contact with the body, especially: pacemakers, internal defibrillators, or other implants (shunts, catheters, metal clips), firmly bonded metallic retainer wires spanning more than four teeth, or fixed metallic braces.
2) Pregnant and breastfeeding individuals.
3) Tattoos on the neck, face, or head.
4) Inability to adhere to the study protocol.
5) Limited or completely abolished legal capacity or a court order for placement.
6) Past history of epileptic seizures.
7) Presence of a severe psychiatric condition such as acute schizophrenia, severe depression, acute suicidality, or drug abuse in the last 2 years.
